A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same change-localization method and PASLCD dataset. Their text, equations, tables and figures, including v2's supplementary material, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MAD-Real and PASLCD experiments, lighting-robustness tests, limited-view evaluations and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds ChangeSim results, supervised-method comparisons and supplementary PASLCD analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 and Figure 2 change the stated change-channel objective from L1 alone to L1 plus D-SSIM. The core representation, mask construction, augmentation and filtering remain unchanged. The supplementary pruning description supplies implementation detail without establishing another procedural change.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on ChangeSim's simulated industrial indoor scenes, expanding coverage beyond MAD-Real's real LEGO objects and PASLCD's real environments. The detailed PASLCD scene inventories document retained coverage rather than establish additional scenes.

E2.justification: PASLCD comparisons add CSCDNet and CYWS-2D in Table 3, plus CYWS-3D in Table 4. ChangeSim Table 2 includes ChangeNet and CSCDNet scores attributed to the dataset paper. The lighting-robustness comparison replaces OmniPoseAD and SplatPose with CYWS-2D, although both remain in the main benchmark.

E3.justification: Added comparisons specify pretrained model sources, aligned rendered pairs and bounding-box-to-mask conversion; ChangeSim adds Change/Static class reporting. The lighting-robustness table now selects methods with overall mIoU at least 0.2. V1's stated AUPR reporting disappears, although no AUPR values were tabulated. Existing binarization thresholds and limited-view splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a test using CYWS-2D masks with Change-3DGS (Table 4) and a focused false-positive/false-negative analysis of mask combination (Figure 7, Section 9.3). Existing spherical-harmonics and component ablations and limited-view analysis remain. Lighting robustness moves to the supplement with revised comparator selection.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three random trials for the limited-view experiment in Section 5.3 and Figure 4. V2 introduces no additional run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: Retained MAD-Real and PASLCD scores are unchanged, including the proposed method's PASLCD mIoU/F1 of 0.461/0.612. V2 adds ChangeSim scores of 0.407/0.918 for Change/Static, supervised-comparator results, lighting-specific scores and a CYWS-2D fusion result increasing mIoU from 0.273 to 0.393 within v2. CYWS-2D F1 is inconsistently listed as 0.398 in Table 3 and 0.388 in Table 4.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Gaussian representation and Equations 1–4 retain their mathematical content. Neither version contains formal guarantees or proofs; the added mechanism explanations do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The three central claims remain: strong localization, unseen-view prediction and complementary feature/SSIM masks. V2 additionally claims that Change-3DGS can extend any change-mask generator to multiple views. The abstract's F1 advantage changes from 1.6× to 1.5× with the expanded comparator set.

C2.justification: Sections 7.1–7.2 explain why separate opacity and reference initialization preserve representations of missing objects. Sections 5.2 and 9.3 add interpretations of supervised-baseline distribution shift and mask-combination failures, including missed structure-aware detections. Conversely, v1's discussion of AUROC imbalance and the Feature Difference baseline's AUROC advantage is removed.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents 7000/3000/3000 training iterations, an RTX 4090 GPU, the two-opacity pruning rule, annotation procedures and detailed scene-change inventories. The code/data release promise becomes a statement of availability with new project-site information. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures; the budgets are not established as changed from v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds ChangeSim and Supervisely references and removes the precision–recall-versus-ROC reference. Previously cited pairwise scene-change methods receive greater comparative emphasis, while the main positioning relative to OmniPoseAD and SplatPose remains.

P1.justification: Most introduction and methodology prose is retained with local editing and author/header updates. Dataset discussion is reordered, single- and multi-object results are consolidated, Section 5.2 becomes the pairwise comparison, and lighting robustness moves to the supplement. New supplementary sections organize supporting details.

P2.justification: V2 expands the PASLCD table with comparator columns and scene-category shading, updates the pipeline and qualitative panels, and adds ChangeSim and pairwise-comparison tables. The supplement adds an augmentation diagram, dataset histograms, annotated failure cases, scene inventories and lighting-specific tables and visualizations. The earlier robustness table is relocated and revised.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps in v1's comparative validation and reproducibility through an external scene-level benchmark, relevant supervised comparators, explicit training and pruning details, and documented annotation procedures. Supplementary failure analysis also clarifies applicability. The new CYWS-2D F1 inconsistency and removal of the AUROC discussion weaken reporting, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
